blind.description: No text or labels are visible in any of the renders. The model is an architectural flying buttress piece composed of a tall upright rectangular pier on the right and a thick curved half-arch sweeping down to a low square footing block on the left, leaving a clear open archway beneath it. The tall pier features a stepped plinth base, moulded capital, and front relief carvings depicting a stylized anvil and geometric forge motifs. The thick arch rib sweeps downward like a stylized hammer handle terminating at the stout blocky footing (resembling a smith hammer head), accented with transverse raised bronze/metal collar bands. Surfaces are solid, manifold, and continuous, with no broken shards, spikes, blobs, holes, or thin floating flakes. There are no hovering unattached parts and nothing melted or fused. The structure stands entirely on its own two integrated rectangular footing bases whose undersides sit flat against the floor, with no added slab, disc, or plinth. Materials and colors consist of dark charcoal/iron-grey stone or weathered metal with warm ember-orange, rust, and antique bronze decorative relief inlays and edge highlights. There are no large plain black or unpainted areas, and no flame or glow.
blind.from_above: From straight above (tile C), the model appears as a straight, thick rectangular beam connecting two wider rectangular blocks: the capital of the tall pier on the right and the lower footing block on the left, with a raised transverse collar band around the middle. The curved arch profile and the open space underneath are clearly visible in the cast shadow on the floor.
blind.height_vs_figure: The tall pier stands approximately 5 to 5.5 ft tall (slightly shorter than the 5 ft 9 in figure, reaching around shoulder level), and the total span across the floor is about 6 to 7 ft wide (slightly longer than the figure is tall).
